basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Prius autem quam irent cubitum, viri civitatis vallaverunt domum, a puero usque ad senem,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Prius autem quam irent cubitum, viri civitatis vallaverunt domum, a puero usque ad senem, omnis populus simul; vocaveruntque Lot, et dixerunt ei: Ubi sunt viri qui introierunt ad te nocte; educ illos huc, ut cognoscamus eos, etc. Hoc est quod propheta Isaias de populo Israel supra modum peccante ait: Peccatum suum sicut Sodoma praedicaverunt nec absconderunt (Isai. III, 9). Peccatum quippe suum sicut Sodomitae praedicaverunt, nec absconderunt, cum absque respectu pudoris alicujus omnes a puerili aetate usque ad ultimam senectutem masculi in masculos turpitudinem operari solebant, adeo ut ne hospitibus quidem ac peregrinis sua scelera abscondere, sed et hos, vim inferendo, suis similes facere sceleribus atque suis facinoribus implicare contenderent.
